calls.head: Daccord gets another crack at the Wild
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Daccord has been shaky against the Wild, well below his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if he’s back to his usual self.

calls.head: The Wild should tilt the ice
calls.body: The Wild have been near the top of the league at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Kraken near the bottom. Expect the Wild to spend more of the night in the Kraken’s end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

SEA.head: We gave Seattle only a 34% chance, and it went the way we feared.

MIN.head: We gave Minnesota a 66% chance, and they delivered.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Wild pile it on the Kraken
paras: Kirill Kaprizov opened the scoring for the Wild just 26 seconds into the game. Berkly Catton made it 1-1 for Seattle midway through the first, but the Kraken didn’t score again. The Kraken went nearly 19 minutes without a shot on goal, from early in the second to early in the third, while the Wild put 15 on net. Most teams don’t go that long without a shot even once a season. Blake Coleman restored the Wild’s lead early in the second, and Olli Määttä scored his first goal for Minnesota midway through the period to make it 3-1. Joel Eriksson Ek made it 4-1 a minute and a half later. Coleman scored again into the empty net with less than four minutes left.

The Wild earned this one. Replay the chances a hundred times and they win about seven in ten. Jesper Wallstedt made 23 saves for the Wild, and Joey Daccord stopped 31 of 35 at the other end. The Wild improved to 7-3-2, second in the Central, while the Kraken dropped to 7-4-1, third in the Pacific.

items.text: Matt Boldy extended his point streak against Seattle to ten games.
The Wild have beaten the Kraken six straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
The Wild bounced back after two straight losses.
Quinn Hughes is now one point from 500.
